parsed.explanation: The combined regime imposes universal exposure at the border and in government facilities. National binary-sex document rules, refusal of X/mismatched markers, possible lifetime fraud findings, and division-level single-sex-space policy mean an outed visitor can be refused entry, stranded, or excluded. If detained or arrested, birth-sex custody placement is documented, with severe abuse and judicial refusal to protect. Division care bans affect a travelling minor and guardian. National hate-crime coverage, marriage recognition and pending litigation are real but do not operate as visitor-facing remedies. The result is High Risk: worse than administrative-exclusion anchors because custody harm and facility exclusion are documented, but not the execution-tier extreme.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-sex order, no new X markers, refusal of X/mismatched markers, discrepancy refusal and possible lifetime fraud finding, trans-athlete entry ban. Outed visitor risks refusal, passport retention, stranding.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; litigation and legal-aid FAQ; fraud finding is not automatic and requires four elements. No documented visitor-facing guarantee.
entry_documents.interaction: Border screening can move from document discrepancy to refusal or permanent ineligibility; division marker rules do not govern foreign passports but signal hostile local practice.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans men; national corrections conversion-like policies; division houses by birth sex and dismissed a failure-to-protect claim after cellmate assault.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; some orders are enjoined. No documented custody protocol protects trans visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest or immigration hold leads to birth-sex placement, where documented harm and no effective remedy follow.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities matching identity; division order backs single-sex bathrooms and changing rooms. Parent map shows many state bans; division enforcement provision not documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No visitor-facing facility protection documented; some private or local settings may differ.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Government buildings, transport and hospitals can exclude; division order reinforces local practice even without a documented criminal bathroom trigger.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care under 19; an adult with a minor cannot obtain it locally. National rules target funding and minors' care; emergency-care discrimination is not documented.
care_services.protection: Adult routine care is not shown restricted by the division; national hate-crime and anti-discrimination rules do not secure care access.
care_services.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces care denial; an adult alone may face administrative friction but no documented care ban.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders equate gender ideology with harm, direct prosecution of teachers aiding social transition, and counterterrorism language names radically pro-transgender groups; official hostility raises reporting and outing risk.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National gender-identity hate-crime law; courts have blocked some orders; no division-wide gender-identity hate-crime or anti-discrimination statute.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile framing makes police or agency contact riskier, though a national hate-crime charge remains available.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-19 care ban in the division; national order threatens prosecution of teachers using preferred names or pronouns; school and facility rules segregate by birth sex. A parent seeking care for a minor has no lawful local route.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented protection for a trans minor visitor; national marriage and adoption recognition are irrelevant here.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling with a trans minor creates care-denial and possible institutional scrutiny; an adult alone avoids this axis.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-level trans violence statistics in the dossier; national climate is hostile. Division hate-crime law omits gender identity; local ordinances are uneven.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; some municipal anti-discrimination ordinances; no documented police protection for trans visitors.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: An outed visitor facing street hostility may get national hate-crime coverage but limited local recourse; no systematic street targeting of visitors is documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Entry and custody policies are in litigation; enforcement varies; the division lacks statewide gender-identity anti-discrimination and its courts dismissed a trans prisoner's claims.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National hate-crime law, marriage recognition, legal-aid FAQ and some local ordinances; fraud finding is not automatic.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are partial and slow; they do not prevent border exclusion, facility denial or custody harm in real time.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor is administrative exclusion with invasive review but no imprisonment. This dossier is worse because national entry can yield refusal and a lifetime fraud finding, and custody includes documented sexual assault, though it lacks that anchor's extortion pattern.

That anchor has an ombudsman-secured release after hours. No comparable visitor remedy is documented here at the border or in custody; facility exclusion and birth-sex custody placement are additional exposures.
That anchor shows a care policy protecting the visitor after staff friction. Here care is banned for minors and no facility or custody protection is shown to operate; the rating is materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines national border/document hostility with division-level single-sex-space policy and birth-sex custody. A visitor is exposed first at entry, where a mismatch can trigger refusal, detention, or a fraud finding. If she enters government facilities or is detained, exclusion or birth-sex placement follows, with documented assault and judicial refusal to protect. National hate-crime coverage and marriage recognition do not function as real-time safeguards. A trans minor travelling with a guardian faces an additional care ban. The rating sits in High Risk, below administrative-exclusion anchors but above execution-tier regimes.
